---
title: "Glossary"
description: "The words Thermite uses, each in a sentence or two, with the page that explains it."
type: reference
sidebar:
  order: 17
---

Thermite's work is organized as **campaign › run › lane › trial › attempt**. A **campaign** says what to improve or achieve. A **run** is that campaign at work on one **rig**. Inside a run, each **lane** is one line of search, worked by a series of **trials**, and a trial may submit one change: an **attempt**. The **judge** gives every attempt a **verdict**. The dashboard follows the same order: campaigns first, then each run with its rig, lanes and attempts.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Advisor** | One of the models the supervisor runs to watch over the research. Together they are **the advisors**: the teachers (with their merged by model), the auditor, the review panel, the synthesizer and the final writer. Advisors never judge. They are off until you configure them: an advisor runs only when it has a model, from the advisors file or from **Edit rig**, MCP or the REST API. Its switch on **Edit rig** is on by default, but a switch alone runs nothing; the synthesizer and the final writer have no switch of their own, and with no model of their own use the first teacher's. The teachers, the auditor and the review panel read the owner's messages to them and answer in **Live**. The teachers and the auditor can also add experiments to the run's queue, and every advisor but the synthesizer and the final writer may keep field notes. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md) and the [advisors file](advisors-file.md) |
| **Agent** | An AI model at work inside a rig: a worker or the planner (**the work**), or an advisor (**the advisors**). Agents propose; they never judge. See [Agents, lanes and the planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md) |
| **Agent token** | A token for a coordinating agent over MCP: it may read and steer, but not message agents, change a run's experiment queue, remove rules, read or grant the knowledge base's collections, or approve anything. See [Tokens and roles](tokens.md) |
| **Answer card** | In a research run, the current answer to one question: a few paragraphs, a certainty (`high`, `moderate`, `low`, `insufficient` or `none`), the verified claims it cites, and its open gaps, each a gap in the evidence or one only a measurement could settle. The supervisor's synthesizer writes them; the harness keeps each question's card as versions and checks each new one in code before it keeps it; workers read the cards in their brief and in `cards/q<index>.md` of the research folder, and never write them. Every report opens with them. See [Answer cards](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#answer-cards) |
| **Answer check** | In a research run, the check that ends it: after the minimum duration, at a digest, code checks that every question has an answer card (and the run has the campaign's floor of verified claims, `min_verified_claims`, when it sets one) and that some question or required hypothesis has no decision that stands, then the review panel decides each such item by a majority, and code checks each answer's citations and numbers. A review that leaves every question with an end ends the run, and so does the progress rule: the final writer writes its research paper, which leads its final report. The run's **Overview** says where it stands. See [When a research run ends](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#when-a-research-run-ends) |
| **Approach family** | A named direction of work, such as `loop-tiling`, that experiments belong to and that directives name. The planner makes up new ones as it plans; a directive may name a new one too, and the planner designs it at its next round: it says what it means, in its own words. A name is 2 to 41 lowercase letters, digits and dashes, written in plain words or as `:name:`: `:Loop tiling:` is `loop-tiling`. An experiment whose direction is in words belongs to the family those words make: "Loop tiling" is `loop-tiling`. A family becomes *exhausted* when a "not possible" proposal counts it as refuted. See [Agents, lanes and the planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#the-planner) |
| **Archived** (campaign) | A campaign the owner took out of the dashboard's left navigation, **Needs you** and the Overview's lists, with **Archive** under **⋯** on its page, `archive_campaign` over MCP or `POST /v1/campaigns/<campaign>/archive`. Its runs, results, kits and collection in the knowledge base stay, it keeps its folder in the navigation, and **Campaigns › Archived** lists it, with **Unarchive**, which brings it back into that folder. Control archives none while a run of it is at work or waits to start, and starts or resumes no run of an archived one. See [Archive campaigns and sort them into folders](../how-to/campaigns/archive-and-folders.md) |
| **Attempt** | One submitted change. Thermite keeps every attempt with its parent, its change, its record and its verdict, even one that loses. An attempt belongs to its run, and is addressed through it: its page is `/ui/campaigns/<campaign>/runs/<run>/attempts/<attempt>`, `GET /v1/runs/<run>/attempts/<attempt>` and MCP's `get_attempt` read it. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md) |
| **Audit** | A second look at a result before it can become the champion: for a surprisingly large gain, a change whose agent declared flaws, or a goal campaign whose contract has an adversarial checklist, on a rig with an auditor. The auditor's clear is the last step before the champion; its block stops the result. A rig with no auditor skips it, and records that. See [Decide what waits for you](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md#audits) |
| **Auditor** | The advisor that answers audits: it clears a result, blocks it, or leaves it to the owner. Without one, there are no audits. When it has a doubt it can't settle, it may also put one check at the top of the run's experiment queue. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md#the-auditor) |
| **Back-pressure** | Limits that hold new work until earlier work settles, such as at most 4 open attempts in a run. Work waits; nothing ends. See [Limits and pacing](limits-and-pacing.md#back-pressure) |
| **Baseline** | A hill climb's first judge job and what it records: the judge measures the run's starting point alone on every case, in 3 blocks, and keeps each case's median and spread for every metric. No round or trial starts before it, and each guard's total allowance holds against it. The run page's **Where the run started** shows it. See [The baseline](contract.md#the-baseline) |
| **Block** | One round of timing: every case runs for the change and for the champion, in a random order, on the same device. The judge decides from many blocks. See [Why agents never judge](../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md) |
| **Brief** (a campaign's) | What a campaign's author tells its agents: additional information, starting links, ideas to try and hypotheses, kept in its contract and set on **2 The brief** of **New campaign**. The agents weigh it as starting points, not rules. Not the same as a briefing. See [The campaign's brief](contract.md#the-campaigns-brief) |
| **Briefing** | Background for every agent of a new run: findings, claims, notes and reports the owner picked from past research when starting it, each with where it came from. Each agent's brief shows it as data, not instructions. It is fixed once the run starts. See [Briefings](knowledge-base.md#briefings) |
| **Broker** | The part of the harness that runs as root and starts every build, run and agent command as its own user. See [Isolation inside a rig](../explanation/isolation.md) |
| **Budget** | A cap a contract may set: wall-clock hours, device hours or model spending. None is set by default; when one is spent, the run is paused. See [Set a budget or a stop time](../how-to/campaigns/budget-and-stop-time.md) |
| **Calibration** | The judge times the champion against itself (an A/A test) to learn how noisy the device is. A hill climb's later decisions never assume less noise than this. See [Limits and pacing](limits-and-pacing.md#the-judge) |
| **Campaign** | One piece of research: what to improve or achieve, and how to judge it, set out in its contract. It runs in one of three modes. Its runs share one collection in the knowledge base. A copy of a campaign has the same contract and kit under another name, with its own empty collection. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md) and [Compare two models from zero](../how-to/campaigns/start-from-dashboard.md#compare-two-models-from-zero) |
| **Cap** | A limit that can stop a campaign's agent work, such as a budget. Caps are off unless someone sets them. See [Limits and pacing](limits-and-pacing.md#caps) |
| **Case** | The dashboard's word for a **cell**: one test case of the kit, such as one input size. The **New campaign** page lists them under **Test cases**. See [Kit manifest](kit-manifest.md) |
| **CDI** | The Container Device Interface: a file that tells Podman which device files make up each GPU. NVIDIA's container toolkit writes it, and rigs on machines get their GPUs through it. See [Compatibility](compatibility.md) |
| **Cell** | One test case the kit can measure, such as a matrix of a given size: a name and its parameters under `cells` in `kit.json`. The contract picks the cells a campaign is judged on, and the dashboard calls them **cases**. See [Kit manifest](kit-manifest.md) |
| **Champion** | A run's best confirmed result so far. It starts as the seed (champion #1), and only the judge's confirmed verdicts replace it, each with the next number, so the first improvement is champion #2. See [How a change becomes the champion](../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md#how-a-change-becomes-the-champion) |
| **Champion patch** | A champion as a git patch against the seed, which you can download and apply to your project. See [Take the result](../how-to/campaigns/take-the-result.md) |
| **Check (kit's)** | The kit's program that reads one run's output and says whether it passed, for example that the result is correct. It runs as part of the judge. In `kit.json`, a run passes only when the check's last line is a JSON object with `"pass": true`; a check described on the **New campaign** page passes when it exits 0. See [Kit manifest](kit-manifest.md#check-output) |
| **Claim** | A statement backed by exact quotes from sources the harness fetched. Research workers record them, and so may hill-climb and goal workers. It counts as verified only when every quote is found word for word and every number in it appears in its quotes; otherwise it is a draft, with its problems, which the run's **History** shows. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research) |
| **Close run** | **⋯** › **Close run** in the header of a running or paused run's page; the command `close_run`, the owner's only. The run ends for good with the owner's reason, as a run that met its goals does: its trials stop, nothing new starts, its jobs waiting for the judge never run, and it can't be resumed. Its results stay. See [Close a run](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#close-a-run) |
| **Collection** | One campaign's part of the knowledge base, made with the campaign: what its runs recorded, under each run, in each writer's **slot**, with its time. A campaign's agents read its own collection and the collections it was granted, read only. Not a folder in the dashboard's left navigation (below). See [Collections](knowledge-base.md#collections) |
| **Compaction** | What happens near a model's context window: Thermite keeps the agent's whole conversation as a document (a worker's or the planner's in the run's research folder, `compactions/`; an advisor's with the supervisor's records), replaces the older turns with a summary that names it, and the agent goes on. By default at 80% of the window; `compact_at`, set with each agent's model or by the campaign, changes it. It never ends a trial. OpenCode v2, Codex and Claude Code compact in their own way, with the settings Thermite gives them; Thermite keeps their conversation too, through Claude Code's PreCompact hook, Codex's own record of the thread and Thermite's OpenCode plugin, and tells their summary to name the file. See [Compaction](limits-and-pacing.md#compaction) |
| **Completed** | The dashboard's word for a closed goal run that met its goals: its newest goal report met every required goal, and the judge's second check agreed. A closed research run whose questions the review panel found answered (`every question is answered`) is Completed too. It shows on the run's page, in **Live** and under **Earlier runs**, and a campaign whose newest run completed shows it in the sidebar, even with an older run paused. Any other closed run is **Finished**. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#run-labels-on-the-dashboard) |
| **Confirmation** | The judge's second measurement of a change that looked better: fresh blocks, decided on that new data alone, plus the held-out cells. See [How a change becomes the champion](../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md#how-a-change-becomes-the-champion) |
| **Context window** | How much a model reads in one request, in tokens: the conversation so far and the reply. Control takes it from the provider's model list. The owner can cap it for each agent's model on a rig, and a campaign can set its own for all its runs' agents ([`agents_context`](contract.md#agents-context)): the lower wins. For example, to compare two models at the same window. Near it, an agent's conversation is compacted (see **Compaction**) and the agent goes on. See [Cap the model's context window](../how-to/models/connect-a-provider.md#cap-the-models-context-window) |
| **Contract** | The file that says what a campaign must achieve and how it is judged: its mode, metrics or goals, editable paths, cases and limits. Each change gets a new version number. See [Contract](contract.md) and [Write a contract](../how-to/campaigns/write-a-contract.md) |
| **Control** | The one central service that shows and steers every rig: the dashboard, the REST API, MCP and the command queues. See [How the parts fit together](../explanation/how-it-fits-together.md) |
| **Copy** (of a campaign) | A new campaign with another name and the same contract and kit as a campaign control keeps, with its own empty collection in the knowledge base and no runs, so that its runs start from zero. **Copy**, beside **Start a run** on the campaign's page, makes one; so do `thermite campaign copy`, `POST /v1/campaigns/<campaign>/copy` and MCP's `copy_campaign`. A research campaign's copy can give its agents other MCP servers. See [Compare two models from zero](../how-to/campaigns/start-from-dashboard.md#compare-two-models-from-zero) |
| **Cross-verified** | A champion that another rig's own judge measured and promoted, after it was sent there by propagation. The leaderboard shows which rigs cross-verified each champion: the dashboard's address `/ui/leaderboard`, `GET /v1/leaderboard` and the MCP tool `leaderboard`. On a campaign's page, such a run under **Earlier runs** shows `cross-verified on` and the rigs, and a hill climb's page links to the **leaderboard**. See [Run a campaign on several rigs](../how-to/campaigns/several-rigs.md) |
| **Development run** | An agent's own run of a command on the measuring device, to test or profile its change. It never counts as a result. See [Sharing a device](../explanation/sharing-a-device.md) |
| **Device** | What a rig measures on: a GPU, or the rig's CPUs. A rig with several GPUs can give some to the judge and some to the agents. See [Sharing a device](../explanation/sharing-a-device.md) |
| **Direction** | Another word for an approach family: the line of work an experiment belongs to, such as `loop-tiling`, or a few words such as "loop tiling". A rule names one, in plain words or as `:loop tiling:`. A run's directions, with what each holds, are on its **Planner** tab (**The run's directions**), the REST API and MCP. A lane tends to keep its last direction, so it builds on what it learned. See [The planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#the-planner) |
| **Directive** | A recorded instruction that steers the planner, with its reasons and sources; it never changes a verdict. The dashboard calls directives **rules**. Its kinds are `avoid`, `try`, `mandate` (**Always** on the dashboard), `priority`, `lane_count`, `trial_minutes` (one trial's length, 1 to 1,440 minutes), `keep_working` (`on` or `off`) and `note`. An `avoid`, `try` or `mandate` directive names a direction; an old one in words (`match`), from before directives named directions, stays in force as legacy, for the planner's model only, until the planner's next round converts it to a directive on a named direction. The owner, the teachers and the planner set them; the planner only when an owner's message asks for one. A directive the owner removed is left out of the teachers' and the planner's later sets; only a `redirect` sets it again. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md) |
| **DRA** | Dynamic Resource Allocation: a Kubernetes way to give pods devices, such as GPUs, through a device class like `gpu.nvidia.com`. A cluster rig gets its GPUs through DRA or through NVIDIA's device plugin. See [Add a rig on a Kubernetes cluster](../how-to/install/rig-on-a-cluster.md) |
| **Duplicate** | An attempt that makes the same change as an earlier attempt of its run. It is kept but not judged again. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#attempt-states) |
| **Earlier run** | A run whose rig is retired, or that ran before its rig's [full reset](../how-to/operate/rig-lifecycle.md#fully-reset-a-rig). Control keeps its events, so it stays on its campaign's page, under **Earlier runs**, marked `on <rig>, retired` or `before <rig>'s full reset`, and opens like any run, with its attempts, history and champions' patches. It runs no more and takes no commands |
| **Enrollment code** | A one-time code control makes for a rig in pull mode, given to its pod at launch. Control and the pod each prove that they hold it, without sending it, when control pins the pod's keys; then it is spent. It expires only when the launch sets an expiry. See [Enrollment](../explanation/trust.md#enrollment) |
| **Epoch** | One round of planning: the planner gives each lane an experiment, and each lane runs its trials. It ends once every free lane has run them; a lane still on a long trial joins the next one. The dashboard calls it a **round**. Contract fields, such as `lanes.trials_per_epoch`, and the workers' briefs keep the word epoch; the live lines say round, as in `planning round 4 (2 lanes)`. See [Agents, lanes and the planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md) |
| **Every detail** | The folded part of the **What it runs on** block on a rig's page. Open it for the rig's full hardware: each device with what uses it (**Used by**), and the CPUs, memory, disks and toolchain. See [Give a rig several GPUs](../how-to/install/several-gpus.md) |
| **Experiment** | One thing for a lane to try: a title, and optionally details, a direction and why. The owner, the planner, the teachers and the auditor add them to a run's experiment queue; the lanes propose them as ideas. One trial works on one experiment, which is then done, with its attempt or why there is none. An experiment can also be dropped, with why. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md) and [Experiment states](verdicts.md#experiment-states) |
| **Experiment queue** | A run's experiments still to try, in order (**Up next**), with the lanes' ideas and what was tried. Each run has its own, kept in the harness's ledger, and the run page's **Experiments** tab shows it, called **Tasks** on a research run's page, where its items are research tasks. The planner gives the first ones to free lanes, never one to two lanes. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md) |
| **Export** | A bundle the harness writes every hour when anything new happened: new events, attempts, champion patches, a snapshot of the ledger, the field notes, research notes and briefings since the last export, and the research folders of finished runs. A full export also holds every run's research folder, finished or not, and each run's archive of the pages it fetched. The supervisor pushes it to the results repository, or, for a rig without one, sends it to control, whose **Exports** page downloads it as one archive. See [Exports](exports.md) and [Set up the results repository](../how-to/operate/results-repository.md#what-gets-pushed) |
| **Fallback** | The fixed rules that give out work when the planner has no model, is off, or gives no usable plan: each lane takes the next queued experiment, **Always** directions first, then **Try** directions, and none that an **Avoid** rule names. Every rule names a direction, so every rule applies; only an old rule in words needs the planner's model. When the queue has nothing for a lane, or for an **Always** direction, the fallback adds an experiment. **Live** and **History** say the round's work went out by the fixed rules, and why. See [The planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#the-planner) |
| **Field note** | A short note an agent keeps as it works: an observation, a decision and why, a surprise, an open question or a lesson, and what it is about. Workers, the planner and the advisors write them; nobody edits or deletes one. What was tried and its result are in the experiment log instead. See [Field notes](knowledge-base.md#field-notes) |
| **Final writer** | The advisor that writes a research run's paper once the review panel's pass of the run is accepted, with its own model from **Edit rig**, or else the model of the rig's first teacher. It reads the run's research, read only, checks its drafts with `check_paper` and `ste_check`, and gives the paper and its next experiments; code decides whether the paper is accepted. Without a model of its own, a rig with no teacher, or with its teachers switched off on **Edit rig**, has none. See [The research paper](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#the-research-paper) |
| **Finding** | In a research campaign, a conclusion a worker records with a summary, why it matters and the verified claims behind it. Code accepts it only when every claim it cites is verified and every number in it appears in those claims; otherwise it stays a draft finding. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research) |
| **Finished** | The dashboard's word for a closed run that did not complete, on its page, in **Live** and under **Earlier runs**: one that ended as not possible, reached the end of its research time, or that the owner closed with **Close run**. A goal run that met its goals, and a research run whose questions were found answered, read **Completed** instead. A finished or completed run takes no more work, messages or decisions: nothing in it waits for you. With no run at work, a campaign is finished when its newest run is closed. In **Tried**, a research task whose trial ended on its own reads "finished:" and its yield, such as "finished: 3 verified claims, 2 from sites new to its question". See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#run-states) |
| **Folder** (in the navigation) | A group of campaigns in the dashboard's left navigation, which the owner names, folds and fills by drag and drop or with **Move to folder** on a campaign's page. It changes nothing else about its campaigns. See [Archive campaigns and sort them into folders](../how-to/campaigns/archive-and-folders.md) |
| **Fork round** | A point where every lane starts again from the champion. With a `budget.wall_hours`, at one third and two thirds of it; without one, every 20 epochs. See [Lane bests and fork rounds](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#lane-bests-and-fork-rounds) |
| **Full reset** | Wiping a rig's state after its results are safely exported, with the owner's confirmation. See [Stop, restart, remove or reset a rig](../how-to/operate/rig-lifecycle.md) |
| **Gap-driven plan** | A research run's plan in code (goal 117): each lane's task goes to the question its answer card weighs for (how open its certainty is, plus its open evidence gaps), with a floor and a ceiling, and none to a question that is decided or saturated. It plans the rounds when the planner is off, and is the planner's fallback. See [How the work is planned](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research) |
| **Gate** | The first step of judging a change in a hill climb: each case runs once, and the change must pass the kit's check. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#attempt-states) |
| **Goal** | In a goal campaign, one thing the result must achieve. A goal is checked by the kit's code, by a measured threshold, or by the review panel. See [Contract](contract.md#goal) |
| **Goal campaign** | A campaign that works until its goals are met. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md) |
| **GPU fence** | The broker's use of the Linux kernel's Landlock feature to stop each role from opening GPUs it may not use. See [Isolation inside a rig](../explanation/isolation.md#gpus-device-groups-and-the-fence) |
| **Grant** | The owner's choice that a campaign's agents may also read another campaign's collection, made on the campaign's page (**Can read from**) or with `kb_grant` over MCP, and removed at any time. See [Grants](knowledge-base.md#grants) |
| **Guard** | A metric that must not get worse while the main metric improves. See [Contract](contract.md) |
| **Hand-out** | The planner's record of which experiment went to which lane, and why: one at the start of each round, and one for each later trial of a lane in the round. The run page's **Planner** tab lists them under **What the planner did**, and **History** has a line for each. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md#see-what-the-planner-did) |
| **Hard constraint** | A limit a change must meet, such as a metric's minimum. A change that breaks one is `infeasible`. See [Contract](contract.md#hill-climb) |
| **Harness** | One of a rig's two containers: it holds the ledger, the judge, the planner, the workers and the broker. It is not the **worker harness**, the program a worker runs in. See [Harness image](harness-image.md) |
| **Held-out cell** | A case the judge runs only at confirmation (a change's, or, in a goal campaign, the champion's second check before the run closes), never while screening, so no agent can tune a change to it. When one fails, the agents learn only that a held-out check failed and how, never which case or its inputs ([Held-out failures](verdicts.md#held-out-failures)). See [Hidden test cases](../explanation/kits.md#hidden-test-cases) |
| **Hill climb** | A campaign that keeps improving a metric. It never ends on its own. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md) |
| **History** | A run page's tab that tells what happened in the run, newest first, in sentences: verdicts, new champions, pauses, how each round's work went out, rules, changes to the queue, hand-outs, claims and more. It shows the newest 400 events. The agents' notes are on the **Journal** tab instead. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md) |
| **Hypothesis** | In a research run, a proposed explanation, tied to a question or to the whole run. The author's, from the campaign's brief, need a verdict from the review panel (supported, refuted or undecided). A worker's goes to the run's **pool**, kept once and changed in place, and needs one only when the owner or the plan promotes it; a repeat of another merges into it, and the owner can retire one. The run page's **Hypotheses** tab lists them all, with **Promote**, **Return to pool** and **Retire**. See [The Hypotheses tab](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#the-hypotheses-tab) |
| **Idea** | An experiment a worker proposes while it works, with `thermite-trial idea` or Pi's `idea` tool; its trial goes on. It waits under **Ideas from the lanes** until the owner or the planner queues it or drops it, or the planner gives it to a lane. The planner's model does that each round; when the queue is below its target (**Ideas kept ready**), the planner queues the distinct ones even without its model. In a research run, ideas wait for the owner. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md#queue-or-drop-the-lanes-ideas) |
| **Ideas kept ready** | A hill-climb or goal campaign's target queue depth: how many experiments each run's queue keeps ready for the lanes, two for each lane unless the campaign sets another (`lanes.queue_target`). A target that drives ideas, not a cap: below it, the planner is asked to top the queue up, and then the teachers. See [Keep ideas ready](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md#keep-ideas-ready) |
| **Inbox and outbox** | Folders a rig's two containers share. The supervisor puts what it fetched in the inbox; the harness writes its exports to the outbox. See [Ports, volumes and secret files](ports-volumes-secrets.md) |
| **Item** (knowledge base) | One thing written in a run's slot of the knowledge base, with its kind, its title and its links to other items: a blurb, a short text, or a file kept whole. A writer may add a new version of its own item; the older versions stay. See [Items](knowledge-base.md#items) |
| **Join command** | A one-time command you run on a machine or cluster to add a rig where control cannot connect. It works once, within an hour. See [Join a rig yourself](../how-to/install/join-a-rig.md) |
| **Journal** | A run's field notes, kept in its ledger. The run page's **Journal** tab shows them, newest first, with filters by writer and by kind, beside the run's research notes and its counts. See [Field notes](knowledge-base.md#field-notes) |
| **Judge** | Code in the harness that builds, measures and checks every change and gives its verdict. Agents can neither read nor change it. See [Why agents never judge](../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md) |
| **Judge only** | A run started with its agents off: no workers run on it, and the judge works alone. Its advisors still work, so experiments can wait in its queue, but no lane takes one. The run's page says so, and its **Experiments** tab says how to carry its experiments to a run with workers. A try of a kit is one kind. See [Judge-only runs](verdicts.md#judge-only-runs) |
| **Kept in force** | An owner's message, to everyone working or to one lane, that every new trial's brief carries until the owner removes it (**📌 N kept** › **Remove** in **Live**, or the command `unkeep_message`). **Live** marks it "📌 kept in force". See [Keep a message in force](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#keep-a-message-in-force) |
| **Kit** | A project's recipe for the judge: how to build, run, time and check it, with its cases and hidden checks. It lives in its own repository, pinned by commit, and agents never see it. See [Why the benchmark lives in a kit](../explanation/kits.md) |
| **Knowledge base** | Thermite's own store of past research, kept by control: one collection for each campaign, with what its runs recorded. The **Knowledge** page in the sidebar shows and searches it. Not the same as the advisors file's `kb`, a search service of your own for the teachers, or an MCP server such as GBrain. See [The knowledge base](knowledge-base.md) |
| **Lane** | One line of search inside a run, worked by one trial after another. Each lane has its own user and its own best result. See [Agents, lanes and the planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md) |
| **Lane best** | A lane's own best win, measured against the current champion, that has not become the champion. The planner can tell a lane to build on it. See [Lane bests and fork rounds](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#lane-bests-and-fork-rounds) |
| **Ledger** | The harness's record of everything that happened on a rig: attempts, verdicts, champions, field notes, each run's briefing, events. Every other view, such as the dashboard, is built from it. See [How the parts fit together](../explanation/how-it-fits-together.md) |
| **Live** (a rig's status) | The green chip a rig shows on **Rigs** when it has reported within the last 180 seconds, by default. Otherwise the chip says **Stale**, **Offline**, **Refused**, **Stopped** (a stopped RunPod pod), **Key to accept** while its key waits for the owner, or **Getting ready** (a RunPod pod before its first report). See [The Rigs list](rigs-list.md#states) |
| **Live** (the sidebar page) | The dashboard page that shows one run at a time as it works: its live view. The list on its left has the runs **At work**, the **Idle rigs** and the runs **Ended in the last day**. With no run chosen, it shows the first run at work; with none at work, it says "No run is at work. Pick one from the list to see its lines." while runs that ended in the last day are listed. See [Send the agents a message](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#send-the-agents-a-message) |
| **Live view** | The dashboard's view of one run's agents, judge and advisors as they work, which adds new lines by itself. Its filters are **Everyone**, one for each lane, **Planner** and **Judge** (except in a research run), **Advisors** and **You** (your messages, who read them and the advisors' answers). Its message box writes to everyone working, a lane, the planner or the advisors; the judge takes no messages. A refused message shows **Not sent.** and the reason above the box. Your messages, read receipts and the advisors' answers show as such only on lines the rig's harness signed; any other line shows as a plain log line. Open it from **Live** in the sidebar, or with **Live** or **Message** on a run's page. A rig's page has its own **Live** button, which shows every session on that rig and links to each run's Live for messages. See [Send the agents a message](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#send-the-agents-a-message) |
| **Machine** | A Linux computer with Podman that control can reach over SSH and set rigs up on. See [Add a rig on a machine over SSH](../how-to/install/rig-on-a-machine.md) |
| **Merged by** | The teachers' model that merges the advice of two teachers into one set of directives, and their experiments and moves for the queue into one list each. One teacher works with no merge; two teachers with no merged by model give the set of the first review that came back. On **Edit rig**, it is the **merged by** line under the second teacher; over MCP and REST, `merged_by`. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md#the-teachers) |
| **Message** (the owner's) | Text the owner sends to a run's agents: to everyone working (every lane at work, and the planner of a hill climb or goal campaign), one lane, the planner, or the advisors (all of them, the teachers, the auditor or the review panel). It is the signed command `message_agent`, sent from **Live** or with the owner's or an operator's token. Control refuses one that nothing on the rig would read, such as one to the planner while it is off. Each reader reads it once, unless it is kept in force. See [Send the agents a message](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#send-the-agents-a-message) and [Signed commands](signed-commands.md#message_agent) |
| **MCP server** | A server of tools from outside Thermite, such as a knowledge base, a code host or a search for papers, that speaks the Model Context Protocol. The owner adds it once in **Settings › Providers › MCP servers**, with how it signs in; a campaign's kit names the servers its workers, planner and advisors use. Control keeps its secret sealed; the rig's harness and supervisor make the calls, so no agent sees the secret. Thermite's own MCP, for people and agents that run campaigns, is another thing: see [MCP tools](mcp-tools.md). See [Give agents MCP tools](../how-to/campaigns/give-agents-mcp-tools.md) |
| **Mode** | The kind of campaign: hill climb, goal or research. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md) |
| **Model file** | A data file your project loads that is not in its repository, such as a machine-learning model's weights. The contract lists each by name and SHA-256 under `models`, and the kit reaches it as `{models:<sha256>}`; it is not the AI model the agents use. The rig's supervisor can download it by URL. See [Contract](contract.md) and [Model files on a rig](model-files.md) |
| **Model route** | Where a rig's agents reach their model: the provider, the model, its key and the worker harness. Control gives it to the rig; without one, the rig's own settings can name a model. See [Connect a model provider](../how-to/models/connect-a-provider.md) |
| **Model usage** | What the agents' model calls used: for each call, its tokens in (with how many came from the provider's cache), its tokens out (with the reasoning among them) and how long it took. Code records each call where it is made, as a `model_call` event of its run; a figure the agent's program does not report is null, never 0. Control sums the records for a run, a campaign or the whole system, today, over 7 days or for all time, with their cost: each call's tokens at its model's price (the provider's list's, else one the owner sets), "on a plan" for a subscription's calls, "no price" where none is known, and a RunPod rig's pod spend. The dashboard shows them at the top of a run's page and on its **Stats** tab, in a campaign page's sidebar and on **Metrics**; REST (`GET /v1/usage`) and MCP (`model_usage`) give them. See [Model use and cost](model-use.md) and [The model usage records](../explanation/how-it-fits-together.md#the-model-usage-records) |
| **Needs update** | The chip in a rig's **Version** on **Rigs** when the rig's version is behind control's, or so old that control refuses it. It opens the rig's page, where **Update to** control's version runs. See [The Rigs list](rigs-list.md#version) |
| **Needs you** | The dashboard's list of everything that waits for the owner: promotions, audits and reviews the run asks the owner about, "not possible" proposals, runs whose agents the model provider stopped (**Agents stopped**), rig keys, wipes, and rigs that stopped reporting (not a RunPod pod that is stopped). It leaves out everything in a closed run: nothing in a finished run waits for you. It is on **Overview**, and its count shows beside **Overview** in the sidebar and in the status bar. See [Decide what waits for you](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md) |
| **"Not possible"** | In a goal campaign, a proposal that the goals cannot be met, made when enough approach families were tried and refuted. It closes the run at once, unless the run asks the owner; then only the owner can accept it. See [Decide what waits for you](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md#not-possible-endings) |
| **Offline** | A rig that has not reported for 15 minutes, by default, or never reported. The REST API, MCP and `thermite rig list` show it as `offline`; **Rigs** shows **Offline**, and the rig's page says `offline`, with a banner. A rig on RunPod whose pod is stopped is **Stopped** on **Rigs** and `stopped` on its page instead. See [Rig versions](rest-api.md#reporting-stale-and-offline) and [A rig's page](rig-page.md#the-reporting-banner) |
| **Operator token** | A token for an agent that runs campaigns for you over MCP: it may read, steer, message agents, change a run's experiment queue and rules, and search the knowledge base and change its grants, but never approve. See [Tokens and roles](tokens.md) |
| **Outside knowledge base** | Before 0.1.0: an MCP server control copied campaign collections to, and that a campaign's teachers could search. At the update, each became an ordinary MCP server. See [Manage MCP servers](../how-to/operate/mcp-servers.md#after-the-update-from-an-outside-knowledge-base) |
| **Overview** | The first page in the dashboard's sidebar: the tallies, **Needs you**, **At work** and **What happened**. A run's page also has an **Overview** tab, the first of its tabs. See [Your first run](../tutorials/first-run.md#4-sign-in) |
| **Owner** | The person who holds the owner's token. Only the owner signs in to the dashboard and approves promotions, reviews and endings. See [Tokens and roles](tokens.md) |
| **Pacing** | Limits that space work out, such as a lane's wait after unproductive trials or a wait after a provider's error. Pacing never ends research. See [Limits and pacing](limits-and-pacing.md#pacing) |
| **Past research** | What a run may read from the knowledge base: the items of its campaign's collection from other runs, and of the collections granted to it. The rig's supervisor syncs them into the run's `knowledge/` folder, which workers search, and which the planner and the advisors search with a read-only tool. See [A run's knowledge folder](knowledge-base.md#a-runs-knowledge-folder) |
| **Portfolio** | The teachers' main product each round: new opportunities for the run's queue, as many as are distinct and evidenced, each with its mechanism, gain bound, smallest experiment and control, stop condition, why it is new, and evidence. Each one becomes an experiment. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md#what-they-answer-a-portfolio-first) |
| **Planner** | A model call at the start of each round, with no memory of its own, that coordinates the run's experiment queue: it gives each lane an experiment, never one to two lanes, and may add, move, drop and accept experiments, each with why. It adds a rule when an owner's message asks for one, and designs each new direction that a rule names. Without a model, when it is off, or when it gives no usable plan, the fallback gives out work. In a research campaign, it plans each round from the questions' answer cards and their gaps, with the gap-driven plan in code as its fallback. See [The planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#the-planner) |
| **Progress rule** | In a research run, the rule that ends a run that has stopped adding: after the minimum duration, when every question still open is saturated and no item improved for a quarter of the running time, the run ends with its open items stated, and its paper. It is not a time cap. See [When a research run ends](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#when-a-research-run-ends) |
| **Promotion** | A change becoming the champion. The **promotion policy** says whether a confirmed win promotes at once (`auto`, the default) or waits for the owner (`owner_approval`); a run's `ask_owner` makes some wins wait. See [Decide what waits for you](../how-to/campaigns/decide-what-waits.md#choose-what-waits) |
| **Propagation** | Sending one rig's champion to another rig's run of the same campaign, where that rig's own judge measures it as an ordinary attempt. See [Run a campaign on several rigs](../how-to/campaigns/several-rigs.md) |
| **Proposer** | A person or script that submits changes to a rig by hand, with the proposer token and `thermite submit`. See [Test a kit with known candidates](../how-to/campaigns/test-a-kit.md) |
| **Protocol** | The version of the contract between control and a rig. Control, each harness and each supervisor report theirs with their Thermite version, and control refuses a rig whose protocol it can't work with. A rig with no protocol is never refused. See [Rig versions](rest-api.md#rig-versions) |
| **Provider** | Something Thermite uses, added once on the dashboard's **Providers** page: a model provider or subscription, a Git access, a machine, a cluster or a GPU cloud. MCP servers have a block of their own on the same page. See [Connect a model provider](../how-to/models/connect-a-provider.md) |
| **Pull mode** | How a rig on RunPod works: its supervisor never connects to control. Control connects to the pod through RunPod's proxy, signs every request, and in each exchange takes the rig's calls and answers them. Everyone else gets an empty 404. See [Rigs in pull mode](../explanation/trust.md#rigs-in-pull-mode) |
| **Queue** | On a run's page, its **experiment queue**. The judge's jobs and control's commands for each rig wait in queues of their own. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md) |
| **Read receipt** | A line in **Live** that shows who read one of the owner's messages, such as "✓ lane-1 read your message: …". A read counts when the reader works with the message: a trial once its agent is at work, the planner once its model's plan is used, the teachers once one gave a review, and the auditor or the review panel once its answer is posted. See [When each agent reads it](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#when-each-agent-reads-it) |
| **Reader token** | A read-only token, for MCP and for scraping `/metrics`. See [Tokens and roles](tokens.md) |
| **Receipt** | A record, written once, of what ran and under what conditions: one for each timed block, kept in the ledger. See [Why agents never judge](../explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md) |
| **Research campaign** | A campaign that gathers sources, verified claims and findings on a topic until the review panel finds its questions answered, or its maximum duration is over; it ends with a research paper. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md) |
| **Research collection** | A run's files, written by the harness from its records and read-only to the workers, who search them. A research run's holds every archived page as text, every claim, finding, hypothesis, note and report section, an index, the newest report, the research paper once there is one (`paper.md`), and a working area for each lane. A hill-climb or goal run's holds the sources, claims and notes its workers recorded, with an index. Every run's has `knowledge/`, its past research, once there is some. See [Campaign modes](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research) |
| **Research paper** | A research run's final paper, written in Simplified Technical English as a normal research paper: an abstract, an introduction, the method, the results, a discussion, the limitations and the future work, in the parts the writer chooses, with each fact citing its verified claims. Code turns each citation into numbered references, such as `[1]`, and appends the References and two appendices: the review panel's decisions (each question's certainty, each hypothesis's verdict, each dissent) and the claims cited. Code accepts it only when every question is answered with its evidence, every cited claim is verified, every number is in the claims it cites or the run's figures, every verdict it gives is one the review panel gave, and the rig's STE checker, when it has one, finds no error. It is `paper.md` in the run's research folder and leads its final report. See [The research paper](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#the-research-paper) |
| **Research note** | A note a worker records with `add_note`, with the sources it relies on, in any mode. It is not a field note: it records what sources say. The **Journal** tab shows research notes in its **Notes** card |
| **Restart the lanes** | **⋯** › **Restart the lanes**, in the header of the run's page or of its Live; the command `reset_workers`: it ends the lanes' running trials and the current round, and every lane starts again from the champion. The experiments they were on go back to the top of the queue. Nothing the judge decided is lost. A run without agents has none. See [Pause, resume or restart the lanes](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md#pause-resume-or-restart-the-lanes) |
| **Results repository** | A git repository where rigs push their exports. See [Set up the results repository](../how-to/operate/results-repository.md) |
| **Review item** | One thing a research review decides: a question's answer card, or a hypothesis that needs a verdict. Each reviewer answers each item, code checks each answer, and the item's decision is the majority of the reviewers whose answer passed, with dissent kept; a tie leaves it open. A question's decision stands until its card changes. See [The Reviews tab](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#the-reviews-tab) |
| **Review panel** | The advisor that reviews a subjective goal without seeing who made the change, and decides a research run's questions and required hypotheses without seeing who found what: two to five reviewers in the advisors file, or three reviewers on one model when its model comes from **Edit rig**, MCP or the REST API. Every reviewer must pass a goal; a research item is decided by the majority of the answers that pass code's check, with the dissent kept. A pass meets the goal, or ends the research run with its final report, unless the run asks the owner to accept it. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md#the-review-panel) |
| **Reviews** (tab) | A research run's tab, and its campaign's: every review of the review panel, newest first, with when it was asked and posted, its tries, what it decided on each item, each reviewer's answers, the owner's messages to it and its cost. See [The Reviews tab](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#the-reviews-tab) |
| **Rig** | Where the research happens: a harness container and a supervisor container, with the device they measure on. A rig works on one run at a time. See [Kits and rigs, side by side](../explanation/kits-and-rigs.md) |
| **Rig check** | A test a rig runs on itself: model route, isolation or smoke. A smoke check makes a campaign named `rig-check-…`, which the **Campaigns** page lists only under its **Rig checks** and **All** filters. See [Rig checks](rig-checks.md) |
| **Rig's file** | What an advisor with no model of its own from control uses: the model the rig's advisors file gives its role. **Edit rig** names it in the first choice of the advisor's **Model** list, such as `rig's file: opus-5.5`, or says `none: off` when the file has none, and then the advisor does not run. In `rig_models`, such an advisor is `null` (the teachers: no models), and `advisors_file` says what the file sets up. See [An agent with no model](../how-to/models/model-per-agent.md#an-agent-with-no-model) |
| **Rig key** | The key a rig's harness signs its reports with. Control trusts it on first contact, or waits for the owner to accept it. See [Accept a rig's key](../how-to/operate/accept-a-rig-key.md) |
| **Rig token** | The token a rig's supervisor uses with control, for its own rig only. See [Tokens and roles](tokens.md) |
| **Role user** | The operating-system user each kind of work runs as inside the harness: `builder`, `run`, `lane-N`, `agent-N` and others. See [Harness image](harness-image.md#users-and-groups) |
| **Round** | The dashboard's word for an **epoch**: one round of planning. Live's header shows the run's round, such as `round 4`. See [Agents, lanes and the planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md) |
| **Rule** | The dashboard's word for a **directive**: **Avoid**, **Try** or **Always** a direction. A run's **Planner** tab lists the rules in force, each with who set it, why, what code does with it now, and **Remove**. On the dashboard, rules come from **Tell the planner**: you say what you want, in plain words or naming a direction as `:shared memory tiling:` (typing `:` lists the run's directions), and the planner makes each rule at its next round. A direction the run doesn't have yet is new, and the planner designs it. Code keeps every rule, with or without the planner's model. A rule you remove stays removed: the teachers and the planner can't set it again, and you can, with `redirect`. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md#make-a-rule-tell-the-planner) |
| **Run** | A campaign at work on one rig, from a starting commit. A run is running, paused or closed (**Completed** or **Finished** on the dashboard); starting a run on a rig pauses the rig's other runs. A run's name, such as `sort-speed-3`, is used once on control, on every rig, so the run is addressed by it under its campaign: `/ui/campaigns/<campaign>/runs/<run>` on the dashboard, `/v1/runs/<run>` over REST, `{run}` over MCP. The rig it ran on is a fact about it, not part of its address. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#run-states) |
| **Run page** | A run's own page, `/ui/campaigns/<campaign>/runs/<run>`, opened from its campaign's page or with **Open the run** in Live; each tab but the overview adds its name, such as `/attempts`. Its header has **Live**, **Message**, **Pause** or **Resume**, **Export** (an export of the rig that holds the run, normal or full), and **⋯**: while the run runs, **Restart the lanes**, and, while it runs or is paused, **Close run**, which ends it for good. A run without agents (a try, a rig check) has no **Message** and no **Restart the lanes**. Its tabs are **Overview**, **Experiments** (the run's experiment queue), **Journal** (the agents' field notes), for a research run **Reviews** (each review of the review panel) and **Hypotheses**, then **Attempts**, **History**, **Planner** (the rules, **Tell the planner**, the hand-outs and the run's directions) and, for a run with agents, **Stats** (its model calls by agent and model). See [Steer a run](../how-to/campaigns/steer-a-run.md) and [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md) |
| **RunPod test pod** | A short test, paid by the hour, that starts the CUDA harness image, or the one-container rig image, on a RunPod GPU to see whether a rig could run there. See [Test a GPU on RunPod](../how-to/install/runpod-test.md) |
| **Saturated** (question) | In a research run, a question whose last 4 finished tasks added no verified claim from a site new to it, and whose answer card's certainty did not rise while they ran (a card rewritten at the same certainty doesn't count). The plan gives it no more tasks, unless every open question is saturated; the progress rule reads it |
| **Scope** (knowledge base) | What a run's agents search in the knowledge base: its campaign's whole collection (continue) or only the run's own items (fresh), and the granted collections it includes. **Start a run** sets it, and it stays so. See [A run's scope](knowledge-base.md#a-runs-scope) |
| **Screen** | The judge's first timing of a change against the champion, in blocks, decided at set points. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#hill-climb) |
| **Seed** | The commit a run starts from. It is champion #1, and the champion patch applies to it. In a hill climb whose seed the judge could not measure, the first setup change it can measure becomes the starting point instead (see **Setup**). For a project in one folder of its repository, the run starts from a commit of that folder alone, made from the seed, and the patch applies to the folder. See [Take the result](../how-to/campaigns/take-the-result.md) |
| **Setup** | A hill climb whose starting point the judge could not measure: it does not build, a case crashes, or the check fails. Its rounds are setup rounds, in which each lane works, with the judge's reasons, to make the project build and run, never changing the kit. The first change the judge can measure becomes the starting point, and its values the baseline. See [The baseline](contract.md#the-baseline) |
| **Sidebar** | The column on the left of every dashboard page: **Overview**, **Campaigns**, **Rigs**, **Metrics**, **Live**, **Knowledge**, **Commands**, **Reports**, **Exports** and **Audit log**; then the campaigns that are not archived, in their folders ([Archive campaigns and sort them into folders](../how-to/campaigns/archive-and-folders.md)); and **Settings** (the cog) and **Sign out** at its foot. See [Your first run](../tutorials/first-run.md#4-sign-in) |
| **Signed command** | An instruction from control to a rig, such as assigning or pausing a run, signed with control's key so the rig can check it. See [Signed commands](signed-commands.md) |
| **Slot** (knowledge base) | Where one writer writes in a run of the knowledge base: `records`, which Thermite's code writes from the run's signed events, or an agent's own, named for its role, with its lane for a worker (`planner`, `worker-1`, `teacher`, …). A writer writes only its own slot. See [The hierarchy](knowledge-base.md#the-hierarchy) |
| **Slot** (cluster) | A Kubernetes namespace the cluster's operators made for Thermite, where control may set one rig up. See [Add a rig on a Kubernetes cluster](../how-to/install/rig-on-a-cluster.md) |
| **Smoke check** | The rig check that runs known changes through the judge and expects each one's known verdict. See [Rig checks](rig-checks.md#smoke-check) |
| **Stale** | A rig that has not reported for 180 seconds, by default. **Rigs** shows it as **Stale**, the rig's page says `stale`, with a banner, and the status bar counts it as stale. A stopped RunPod pod is not stale: it can't report, so the status bar, **Overview**'s tallies, **Live**'s **Idle rigs** and a run's page call it stopped, **Needs you** shows no card for it, and **New campaign** and **Start a run** let you choose it (the run starts the pod first). The REST API, MCP and `thermite rig list` show it as `stale` until it is offline. See [Troubleshoot](../how-to/operate/troubleshoot.md) |
| **Standing decision** | In a research run, the review panel's newest decision on an item, a question or a required hypothesis, while it holds: a question's lasts until its answer card has a newer version, a hypothesis's for good. A question **has an end** when its standing decision is answered or insufficient |
| **Start a run** | The button on a campaign's page that opens a panel to start a new run of the campaign: on which rig, and with agents or as a try. A campaign saved on control starts from its newest version. One assigned over the API, MCP or the command line starts again from its newest assignment, with the same contract, starting commit and imports. With agents on, its **From past research** can start the run from items of the collections the campaign may read; a try hides it. Its twins, `thermite run start`, `POST /v1/campaigns/<campaign>/runs` and MCP's `start_run`, do the same from a script or an agent. See [Start a campaign from the dashboard](../how-to/campaigns/start-from-dashboard.md) |
| **Static checks** | Checks made before a change is built: only editable paths, no forbidden patterns, no binary files, links or submodules. A change that fails is `rejected_v0`. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md#attempt-states) |
| **Status bar** | The line along the bottom of every dashboard page: the rigs, how many are stale and how many RunPod pods are stopped, **Needs you**, the runs at work and the judge's jobs. Pages never reload by themselves: its **refresh** link loads the page again. After a button that sends something to a rig, the page follows it and draws again the parts it changes, with no refresh: see [Signed commands](signed-commands.md#on-the-dashboard). See [Check a rig](../how-to/operate/check-a-rig.md) |
| **Supervisor** | A rig's second container, its link to the outside: it relays reports, commands and the live view to and from control, hands the harness its model route and its workers' and planner's MCP servers, does all git work, and runs the advisors. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md) |
| **Synthesizer** | The advisor that keeps a research run's answer cards current, with its own model from **Edit rig**, or else the model of the rig's first teacher: at each round, it rewrites the card of each question whose evidence changed since its card, from the card and the question's new verified claims, judged against the question's rubric. Code checks each card before the harness keeps it. Without a model of its own, a rig with no teacher, or with its teachers switched off on **Edit rig**, has none. See [The synthesizer](../explanation/supervision.md#the-synthesizer) |
| **Target** | What a rig measures on, reached through a driver: `cpu` or `cuda-gpu` in this version. A kit names the target it needs. See [Kits and rigs, side by side](../explanation/kits-and-rigs.md) |
| **Teachers** | The advisors that review a running run, every hour by default, soon after the owner writes to them, and at once when its queue runs below its target: one or two models, each a **teacher**. Their main product is a **portfolio** of new opportunities for the run's queue, each with its evidence; they recommend directives with their sources only when new evidence calls for one, and may move queued experiments. With two, their **merged by** model merges their advice into one set, and drops no distinct idea. See [Supervision](../explanation/supervision.md#the-teachers) |
| **The work** | The agents in a rig's harness: the workers, which change the code, and the planner, which picks what each worker tries next. The other group is **the advisors**, in the supervisor. See [Agents, lanes and the planner](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md) |
| **Token** | A long random string that identifies a person, an agent or a rig to control or to a harness. See [Tokens and roles](tokens.md) |
| **Trial** | One worker's session in a lane, started from fresh context, on one experiment from the run's queue. It submits at most one attempt, and may propose ideas for the queue and keep field notes. It ends when it submits, when a time limit someone set runs out, or when it stops. A conversation that nears the model's context window is compacted, and the trial goes on. Not the same as a try of a kit. See [One trial](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#one-trial) |
| **Tried** | A run's experiments that ended, newest first, on its **Experiments** tab: each with its attempt and outcome, no attempt and why, who dropped it and why, or a finished research task. Chips filter it: **Wins**, **Not better**, **Broken or blocked**, **Other results**, **Research finished** and **No attempt or dropped**. See [An experiment's result](verdicts.md#an-experiments-result) |
| **Try** (of a kit) | A judge-only run with no agents, started with **Try the kit first** on the **New campaign** page, with **Start a run** and **Agents** › **Off: a try** on a campaign's page, or with `--agents off` on `thermite assign` or `thermite run start`: the judge builds the starting point and measures it, so you see the kit work before agents start. A hill climb's try measures the starting point alone on the visible cases (its **baseline**), then times it against itself to learn the rig's noise; hidden cases are not run. See [Start a campaign from the dashboard](../how-to/campaigns/start-from-dashboard.md) |
| **Up next** | A run's queued experiments, in order, at the top of its **Experiments** tab. The first ones go to free lanes. You can add one, edit one's words, drag one to a new place, move one to the top or drop one. See [Choose what a run tries next](../how-to/campaigns/choose-what-runs-next.md) |
| **Verdict** | The judge's decision on an attempt, such as `win_confirmed`, `neutral`, `regress` or `invalid`. See [Verdicts and states](verdicts.md) |
| **Worker** | The agent that works one trial in a lane: it reads and edits the project, builds and tests, and submits a change, and may record the sources it reads, with claims and notes. In a research campaign, it reads sources and records claims and findings instead. See [One trial](../explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md#one-trial) |
| **Worker harness** | The program a rig's workers run in, which gives the model its tools: Pi (built into the harness), OpenCode v2, Claude Code or Codex (the Codex CLI). It is chosen in **Harness and model for each rig** on **Settings › Providers**, under **Runs in** on **Edit rig**, in **The agents run in**, next to **The agents' model**, on the **New campaign** page, with the MCP tool `set_rig_model`, or with `THERMITE_AGENT_HARNESS` for a rig that keeps its own model. The planner and each advisor with a model of their own run in one of the same four programs, the one their model needs unless **Runs in** on **Edit rig**, `set_rig_model` or its REST twin names another; an advisor's runs in the supervisor, with none of the program's own tools. See [Give each agent its own model](../how-to/models/model-per-agent.md#where-each-agent-runs) |
| **Yield** | What a research task's trial added, kept with the task when it ends: its verified claims by question, how many brought a site new to the question, the sites new to the run, its findings and its changes to answer cards. **Tried** on the run's **Experiments** tab shows it, and saturation is measured from it. See [Research](../explanation/campaign-modes.md#research) |

## Older names

Before 2026-10-15 a rig was called a **unit**, and a run an **instance**. Older ledgers and command-line flags with those names are still read under the new names.
